Increased wildfire occurrence on and near the mine site can be mitigated by utilizing fire fighting personnel and equipment located at the mine site. Water trucks and heavy equipment (bulldozers) are very efficient fire fighting tools and are available at the mine site.
Possible outbreaks of forest insects can be lessened by proper disposal of forest residues. Prompt disposal of slash can be accomplished by burning in accordance with state regulations.
Cropland
Approximately 12% of the surface areas of Tracts II and III have been cultivated. Additional lands have the potential for cultivation but usually the fields are small which may make them economically unfeasible.
In 1975, approximately 700 acres of Tract II and 1,575 acres of Tract III were being cultivated. In addition, 985 acres of Tract II and 680 acres of Tract III had been cultivated previously but had been abandoned or reseeded to grass.
Reclamation of land for cultivation purposes is possible especially since topsoil is available for respreading. However preliminary soils tests by the Montana Testing Laboratories and the Colorado School of Mines indicate there may be saline and alkali spoils which would cause problems for many field crops. Barley is semi-tolerant to salinity and alkalinity and it is also drought resistant. Fertility tests indicate the spoils will be very low in Nitrogen and Phosphorus, and that topsoils in the area also are deficient. Therefore, a soil fertility enhancement program using chemical or organic methods probably would be needed to reclaim these mined lands for farming.
